s441.content:
Menas was an Egyptian soldier in the Roman army who left military service rather than take part in the persecution of Christians. After years of prayer as a hermit, he publicly confessed his faith and was beheaded in Phrygia.

His body was brought back to Egypt, and his shrine at Abu Mena, near Alexandria, became one of the greatest pilgrimage sites of the ancient world. Pilgrims carried home small clay flasks stamped with his image.
s441.intercession: St. Menas, pray for us. Give us courage to confess Christ before all. Amen.

s442.content:
Sergius and Bacchus were officers in the Roman army and close companions. When they refused to enter a temple of Jupiter, they were paraded through the streets in women’s clothing to shame them, and then tortured.

Bacchus died under the lash, and Sergius was beheaded at Resafa in Syria, which became a great pilgrimage city named Sergiopolis. They are among the most honored soldier saints of the East.
s442.intercession: Holy Sergius and Bacchus, pray for us. Make us faithful friends who help each other toward heaven. Amen.

s443.content:
Theodore was a young recruit (tyro means "recruit") in the Roman army at Amasea, in today’s Turkey. He refused to sacrifice to the gods, and according to tradition he set fire to the temple of the mother goddess. He was tortured and burned alive.

St. Gregory of Nyssa preached a panegyric in his honor. On the first Saturday of Great Lent the Byzantine Church remembers a miracle in which he warned the Christians of Constantinople about food sacrificed to idols.
s443.intercession: St. Theodore, pray for us. Help us to be good soldiers of Christ. Amen.

s444.content:
Mercurius was a Roman officer of Scythian descent, honored for his courage in battle. When the emperor Decius commanded a sacrifice to the gods in thanksgiving for victory, Mercurius refused and confessed that he was a Christian.

He was tortured and beheaded at Caesarea in Cappadocia. In icons he is shown as a warrior saint with a sword, and in the Coptic Church he is called Abu Sefein, "the one with two swords."
s444.intercession: St. Mercurius, pray for us. Defend us in our battles against sin. Amen.

s445.content:
Procopius was a reader, translator, and exorcist of the church at Scythopolis in Palestine. He was the first martyr of the Great Persecution in Palestine, beheaded at Caesarea for refusing to sacrifice to the emperors.

His death is recorded by the historian Eusebius, who lived in Caesarea at the time. Later legends made him a soldier, and the East honors him as a great-martyr.
s445.intercession: St. Procopius, pray for us. Help us to love the word of God and to proclaim it faithfully. Amen.

s446.content:
Charalampus was an elderly priest of Magnesia in Asia Minor who was martyred during the persecution of Septimius Severus. According to tradition, he was more than a hundred years old.

He is much loved in Greece, where many churches are dedicated to him, and he is invoked against plague and sickness.
s446.intercession: St. Charalampus, pray for us. Strengthen the elderly, and protect us from sickness. Amen.

s447.content:
Mamas was born in prison to Christian parents who died for the faith. Raised by a Christian widow in Caesarea of Cappadocia, he was martyred as a teenager under the emperor Aurelian.

Tradition says that he lived for a time as a shepherd in the mountains, where wild animals gathered peacefully around him. Sts. Basil the Great and Gregory of Nazianzus both praised him in their sermons.
s447.intercession: St. Mamas, pray for us. Protect young people, and bless all who care for animals. Amen.

s448.content:
Magundat was a Persian soldier in the army of King Khosrow II. Moved by the relic of the True Cross, which the Persians had carried off from Jerusalem, he became a Christian, took the name Anastasius, and became a monk near Jerusalem.

He went to Persia to preach and was arrested, tortured, and strangled with about seventy other Christians. His relics were brought to Rome, to the abbey of Tre Fontane.
s448.intercession: St. Anastasius, pray for us. Draw all people to the Cross of Christ. Amen.

s449.content:
According to a beloved legend, Alexis was the son of a wealthy Roman family who fled on his wedding night to live as a beggar near Edessa in Syria. Years later he came home and lived unrecognized under the stairs of his parents’ house, sharing the scraps of their table.

Only after his death did they discover from a letter in his hand who he was. His story of humility and hidden holiness was told and retold across East and West throughout the Middle Ages.
s449.intercession: St. Alexis, pray for us. Teach us to seek God alone, and to love the hidden life. Amen.

s450.content:
Onuphrius lived alone for sixty years in the desert of Upper Egypt, clothed only in his long hair and a loincloth of leaves, fed by a date palm and, according to tradition, by an angel who brought him the Eucharist.

His story is told by the monk Paphnutius, who found him near the end of his life, heard his account, and buried him. Icons show him as an old man with a long white beard covering his body.
s450.intercession: St. Onuphrius, pray for us. Help us to depend on God alone. Amen.

s451.content:
Arsenius was a learned Roman of senatorial rank who served as tutor to the sons of the emperor Theodosius I. Hearing a voice say "Arsenius, flee from men and you will be saved," he left the court and became a monk in the desert of Scetis in Egypt.

He was known for his tears and his love of silence. One of his sayings in the Sayings of the Desert Fathers is that he had often regretted speaking, but never regretted keeping silent.
s451.intercession: St. Arsenius, pray for us. Teach us the value of silence and prayer. Amen.

s452.content:
Macarius was a confectioner of Alexandria who became a monk and lived for more than sixty years in the deserts of Egypt, among the monks of the Cells. He was famous for his severe fasts and for competing to outdo any ascetic practice he heard of.

He was a priest and the spiritual father of hundreds of monks, and is often remembered together with his namesake, St. Macarius the Great.
s452.intercession: St. Macarius, pray for us. Help us to discipline our bodies and free our hearts for God. Amen.

s453.content:
Theodosius came from Cappadocia to the Holy Land as a pilgrim and stayed to become a monk. He founded a great monastery near Bethlehem, with hospitals and guest houses for the sick, the poor, and the elderly.

He was called "the Cenobiarch," the head of all the monks who lived in community in Palestine, while his friend St. Sabbas led the hermits. Together they defended the Council of Chalcedon.
s453.intercession: St. Theodosius, pray for us. Help us to live together in love and to serve the poor. Amen.

s454.content:
Gerasimus founded a community of hermits near the Jordan River. During the week the monks lived alone in their cells, and on weekends they gathered for the liturgy and a common meal.

According to a famous story, he pulled a thorn from the paw of a lion, which then served the monastery faithfully and died of grief on his grave. Icons show him with the lion at his feet.
s454.intercession: St. Gerasimus, pray for us. Teach us gentleness toward all God’s creatures. Amen.

s455.content:
Daniel was a disciple of St. Simeon Stylites. After Simeon’s death he set up his own pillar near Constantinople and lived on top of it for thirty-three years, exposed to the weather.

Emperors came to him for advice, and once he came down from his pillar to defend the faith of the Council of Chalcedon against the emperor Basiliscus. Crowds came to him for prayer and healing.
s455.intercession: St. Daniel, pray for us. Raise our hearts above the cares of this world. Amen.

s456.content:
Simeon climbed his first pillar near Antioch at the age of seven and spent almost his whole life on pillars on the "Wonderful Mountain" in Syria. A great monastery grew up around him.

He was ordained a priest, and pilgrims came from far away for his counsel and healing. Among his correspondents was the historian Evagrius, who described him.
s456.intercession: St. Simeon, pray for us. Help us to pray without ceasing. Amen.

s457.content:
Isidore was a monk and priest near Pelusium in Egypt, a disciple of St. John Chrysostom. More than two thousand of his letters survive, explaining Scripture and giving spiritual counsel to bishops, officials, and ordinary people.

He wrote boldly to the powerful, including his own patriarch, St. Cyril of Alexandria, urging him to be moderate and fair in the controversy with Nestorius.
s457.intercession: St. Isidore, pray for us. Give us the courage to speak the truth with love. Amen.

s458.content:
Olympias was a wealthy noblewoman of Constantinople who was widowed young. Refusing to remarry, she was ordained a deaconess and gave her fortune to the poor and the Church, founding a community of women and a hospital.

She was a close friend and supporter of St. John Chrysostom. When he was exiled, she was persecuted and exiled too, and seventeen of his letters to her survive.
s458.intercession: St. Olympias, pray for us. Help us to be generous friends and faithful in trials. Amen.

s459.content:
Pulcheria was the granddaughter of Theodosius I and served as regent for her younger brother, the emperor Theodosius II. She vowed herself to virginity and led a life of prayer at court.

She defended the title Theotokos, Mother of God, for the Virgin Mary, and after her brother’s death she and her husband Marcian called the Council of Chalcedon in 451, which proclaimed that Christ is one person in two natures.
s459.intercession: St. Pulcheria, pray for us. Bless those who govern, and help them to defend the truth. Amen.

s460.content:
Martin I was elected pope in 649 and immediately held a council at the Lateran that condemned Monothelitism, the teaching that Christ had only a divine will, against the wishes of the emperor.

The emperor had him arrested, taken to Constantinople, put on trial, and exiled to the Crimea, where he died of hunger and mistreatment. He is the last pope honored as a martyr, and he is venerated in East and West.
s460.intercession: Pope St. Martin, pray for us. Strengthen the successor of Peter, and all who suffer for the truth. Amen.

s461.content:
Tarasius was a layman and imperial secretary when he was chosen as Patriarch of Constantinople in 784. He agreed only on condition that a council be held to restore the veneration of icons.

He presided over the Second Council of Nicaea in 787, the seventh ecumenical council, which taught that holy images may be venerated because the honor paid to an image passes to the one it depicts.
s461.intercession: St. Tarasius, pray for us. Help us to honor Christ and his saints in holy images. Amen.

s462.content:
Nicephorus, like Tarasius, was a layman and imperial official before becoming Patriarch of Constantinople in 806. When the emperor Leo V revived iconoclasm, Nicephorus refused to give in.

He was deposed and exiled to a monastery, where he wrote important works defending the holy icons and a short history of the Byzantine Empire.
s462.intercession: St. Nicephorus, pray for us. Make us steadfast in the faith of the Church. Amen.

s463.content:
Methodius was a monk from Sicily who suffered years of imprisonment for defending the icons during the second period of iconoclasm.

In 843, with the support of the empress Theodora, he became Patriarch of Constantinople and restored the veneration of icons for good. That victory is celebrated every year on the first Sunday of Great Lent, the Sunday of Orthodoxy.
s463.intercession: St. Methodius, pray for us. Help us to endure suffering for the truth with patience. Amen.

s464.content:
Stephen was abbot of a monastery on Mount Auxentius near Constantinople during the first period of iconoclasm. He encouraged monks and lay people to keep venerating the icons.

The emperor Constantine V had him imprisoned. According to his Life, he once threw a coin stamped with the emperor’s image on the ground and asked whether the one who trampled it deserved punishment, showing that dishonoring an image dishonors the person. He was dragged through the streets and killed by a mob.
s464.intercession: St. Stephen, pray for us. Give us courage to defend what is holy. Amen.

s465.content:
Ignatius was the son of a Byzantine emperor. After his father was overthrown, he was made a monk as a boy and later became Patriarch of Constantinople.

He was deposed in 858 and replaced by Photius, which began a long dispute between Rome and Constantinople. Pope St. Nicholas I supported him, and he was restored in 867. He is honored as a saint in both East and West.
s465.intercession: St. Ignatius, pray for us. Heal the divisions among Christians. Amen.

s466.content:
Theophanes was a wealthy nobleman who, with his wife’s agreement, became a monk, and founded a monastery near the Sea of Marmara. He attended the Second Council of Nicaea.

He wrote a Chronicle of world history that is a major source for Byzantine history. When iconoclasm returned, he refused to give up the icons and died in exile after two years in prison.
s466.intercession: St. Theophanes, pray for us. Help us to remember God’s work in history. Amen.

s467.content:
Joseph was a Sicilian-born monk who settled in Constantinople. On a journey to Rome to seek help for the defenders of icons, he was captured by pirates and enslaved in Crete for several years.

He is one of the most prolific Byzantine hymn writers, and many of the canons still sung in the Byzantine services were written by him.
s467.intercession: St. Joseph, pray for us. Teach us to sing God’s praises with all our hearts. Amen.

s468.content:
Plato gave away his fortune, became a monk, and later founded the monastery of Sakkoudion in Bithynia, where his nephew St. Theodore the Studite became a monk under him.

He and Theodore were imprisoned and exiled for opposing the emperor’s unlawful second marriage and later for defending the icons. Theodore preached a funeral oration in his honor.
s468.intercession: St. Plato, pray for us. Help us to guide others in the way of holiness. Amen.

s469.content:
Cyriacus came from Corinth to Jerusalem as a young man and spent more than ninety years as a monk in the Judean desert, in the monastic communities founded by Sts. Euthymius and Sabbas.

He lived to the age of about 109 and defended the Church against the errors attributed to Origen. His life was written by Cyril of Scythopolis, who knew him personally.
s469.intercession: St. Cyriacus, pray for us. Grant us perseverance in prayer to the very end. Amen.

s470.content:
John became bishop of Colonia in Armenia at the age of twenty-eight. After nine years he secretly left his see and went to Jerusalem, where he joined the Great Lavra of St. Sabbas as a simple monk.

When his identity was discovered, he spent the rest of his long life as a hermit in silence and prayer. His life was written by Cyril of Scythopolis.
s470.intercession: St. John the Silent, pray for us. Teach us humility and the prayer of the heart. Amen.

s471.content:
Eucherius was a married nobleman of Gaul who, with his wife Galla, withdrew to the monastery of Lérins and later to a nearby island to live as hermits.

He became bishop of Lyon and wrote In Praise of the Desert and On Contempt for the World, which spread the ideals of monasticism through the Western Church.
s471.intercession: St. Eucherius, pray for us. Help us to keep our hearts free for God amid the cares of the world. Amen.

s472.content:
Maron was a priest and hermit who lived in the open air on a mountain in the region of Cyrrhus, in northern Syria, spending his life in prayer and penance. The bishop and historian Theodoret described his holiness and his gift of healing, and St. John Chrysostom wrote to him from exile asking for his prayers.

His disciples founded monasteries in the valley of the Orontes, and the Maronite Church, which today has millions of faithful in Lebanon and around the world, takes its name from him.
s472.intercession: St. Maron, pray for us. Bless the Maronite Church and all Christians of Lebanon and the Middle East. Amen.

s473.content:
According to Maronite tradition, John Maron was a monk of the monastery of St. Maron who became the first Maronite Patriarch of Antioch at the end of the seventh century.

He led his people in difficult times, when Christians of the region were caught between the Byzantine Empire and the new Arab caliphate, and he is honored as a father of the Maronite Church’s life and liturgy.
s473.intercession: St. John Maron, pray for us. Strengthen the shepherds of the Eastern Churches. Amen.

s474.content:
Estephan Douaihy was sent from Lebanon to study at the Maronite College in Rome as a boy, and returned as a brilliant scholar and priest. He became Maronite Patriarch of Antioch in 1670 and led his Church for more than thirty years.

He reformed and restored the Maronite liturgy and wrote histories of the Maronite people, earning the title "father of Maronite history." He suffered persecution and exile from local rulers, but remained a humble shepherd. He was beatified in 2024.
s474.intercession: Blessed Estephan, pray for us. Help us to love the history and worship of the Church. Amen.

s475.content:
Flavien Michel Malke was a Syriac Orthodox monk who entered into communion with the Catholic Church and became the Syriac Catholic bishop of Gazarta, in what is now southeastern Turkey.

During the genocide of Christians in 1915, he refused to abandon his flock or to deny Christ, and he was killed. He was beatified in 2015, on the hundredth anniversary of his death.
s475.intercession: Blessed Flavien, pray for us. Strengthen the persecuted Christians of the Middle East. Amen.

s476.content:
Ghebre Michael was a learned Ethiopian monk who searched for the true faith. Through his friendship with St. Justin de Jacobis, he became a Catholic, and Justin ordained him a priest.

During a persecution under the emperor Tewodros II, he was arrested, tortured, and dragged in chains for months. After thirteen months of suffering he died by the roadside in 1855. He was beatified in 1926.
s476.intercession: Blessed Ghebre Michael, pray for us. Help us to seek the truth with our whole heart. Amen.

s477.content:
Bartholomew was a Greek-speaking monk from Calabria and a disciple of St. Nilus of Rossano. After Nilus founded the abbey of Grottaferrata near Rome in 1004, Bartholomew completed its building and became its abbot.

He was a gifted writer of Byzantine hymns and the author of the Life of St. Nilus. Grottaferrata still celebrates the Byzantine liturgy today, in full communion with Rome.
s477.intercession: St. Bartholomew, pray for us. Teach us to praise God in beauty and peace. Amen.

s478.content:
Mykyta Budka was the first bishop of the Ukrainian Catholics in Canada, serving from 1912 to 1928. He traveled the prairies by train and wagon to care for the scattered immigrant communities and built up parishes and schools.

After returning to Ukraine, he was arrested by the Soviets in 1945 and sent to a labor camp in Karaganda, Kazakhstan, where he died in 1949. He was beatified in 2001.
s478.intercession: Blessed Mykyta, pray for us. Bless all immigrants and those who care for them. Amen.

s479.content:
Hryhorij Khomyshyn was bishop of Stanislaviv (today Ivano-Frankivsk) for four decades. He was a strong, demanding pastor who worked for the renewal of his people’s faith and morals.

Arrested by the Soviet secret police in 1945, he was interrogated and tortured, and he died in a Kyiv prison in 1947. He was beatified in 2001.
s479.intercession: Blessed Hryhorij, pray for us. Make pastors courageous in teaching the truth. Amen.

s480.content:
Hryhorij Lakota was a priest, scholar, and auxiliary bishop of Przemyśl. When the communists moved to destroy the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church after the Second World War, he refused to join the state-controlled Orthodox Church.

He was arrested in 1946 and sentenced to a labor camp near Vorkuta, beyond the Arctic Circle, where he died in 1950. He was beatified in 2001.
s480.intercession: Blessed Hryhorij, pray for us. Give us steadfastness in the faith. Amen.
